## Summary

This assignment is hands-on practice for Milestone 2:
build a [Docker image]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="A Docker image is a saved snapshot of a computer setup: an operating system, software and packages, ready to run. A container is one running copy of an image. You write the recipe for the image in a Dockerfile."} from a `Dockerfile`, and publish it to [Docker Hub]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="Docker Hub is a website that stores Docker images, the way GitHub stores code. Anyone can download a public image from it. Here you publish your image there, so others can use it without building it themselves."} with [GitHub Actions]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="GitHub Actions runs commands for you on a fresh computer at GitHub when something happens in your repository, such as a push. You write the commands in a workflow file (a .yml file in .github/workflows/). Here it builds your image and uploads it to Docker Hub."}.

- [ ] Make a small uv (Python) **or** renv (R) project with two pinned packages
- [ ] Add a `Dockerfile` that installs your packages, and test it on your computer
- [ ] Publish the image to Docker Hub with a GitHub Actions workflow

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Readings for this assignment

-   [uv: pinning exact versions](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/virtual-environments-python-uv-exact-pins.html)
    or [renv: declaring packages in `DESCRIPTION`](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/virtual-environments-r-renv-description.html)
-   [Python packages with uv in an image](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-uv.html)
    or [R packages with renv in an image](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-renv.html):
    what each line of the `Dockerfile` does
-   uv refresher: [DSCI 521 uv lecture notes](https://ubc-mds.github.io/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/lectures/virtual-environments-uv.html)
:::

## Instructions

1.  **Make the repository.**
    Create a **public** GitHub.com repository under your personal account, named `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`,
    with a `README`. Clone it; everything below happens in this folder.

2.  **Make a small project** with uv **or** renv, whichever you prefer.
    It needs at least **two** packages you haven't used before, each **[pinned to an exact version]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="Pinning means recording one exact version of a package (e.g. pandas==2.2.3), instead of whatever is newest. Everyone who installs your project then gets the same version, so the code behaves the same."}**.

    -   **uv:** `pyproject.toml` lists each package with `==`, and Python 3.11 or newer is pinned in `.python-version`.
        Commit `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `.python-version`, but not `.venv/`.
    -   **renv:** `DESCRIPTION` lists each package with `(== x.y.z)`, using [explicit snapshots]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="A snapshot is when renv writes down your installed packages in renv.lock. With explicit snapshots, renv records only the packages listed in DESCRIPTION (and the packages they depend on), not every package it finds in your code. Turn it on with renv::settings$snapshot.type('explicit')."}.
        Commit `DESCRIPTION`, `renv.lock`, `.Rprofile` and `renv/`
        (the `.gitignore` inside `renv/` keeps the installed packages out).

3.  **Add the `Dockerfile`.**
    Copy the uv or renv version below into a file named `Dockerfile` (no file extension) in the root of your repository.
    It installs your packages exactly as your [lock file]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="A lock file (uv.lock for uv, renv.lock for renv) is generated by your environment manager. It records the exact version of every package your project uses, including the packages they depend on, so the environment can be rebuilt exactly."} records them.
    The comments explain each line. For renv, change `4.6.2` on the `FROM` line to the R version in your `renv.lock`.

4.  **Test it on your computer.**
    Build the image, then load your packages in a container from it (commands below).
    Fix problems now: debugging on your computer is much faster than on GitHub Actions.

5.  **Publish with GitHub Actions.**
    Set up Docker Hub and the two [secrets]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="A repository secret is a password or token saved in your GitHub repository's settings. Workflows can use it, but nobody can read it back, and it never shows up in your code or logs. Here the two secrets let the workflow log in to Docker Hub as you."} (see below).
    Then copy the workflow below into `.github/workflows/publish-dockerhub.yml`,
    and change only its `IMAGE` line to `<your-docker-hub-username>/dsci522-dockerfile-practice`, all in lowercase.
    Commit and push.

6.  **Check that it worked.**
    The run on the **Actions** tab finishes with a green check mark,
    and your Docker Hub repository shows two [tags]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="A tag is a label on a Docker image, written after a colon (e.g. python:3.14-slim). One image can have several tags. Here latest always points to your newest image, and the sha- tag names the commit that built it."}: `latest` and `sha-` plus 7 characters.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The `Dockerfile` (step 3)

::: panel-tabset
## uv (Python)

```{.dockerfile filename="Dockerfile"}
# Adapted from docker-uv-renv by Daniel Chen (MIT License)
# https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv

# Start from Ubuntu Linux. It has no Python: uv installs it.
FROM ubuntu:24.04

# Copy the uv program into the image (0.13.7 pins uv's version)
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.7 /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/

# Work in the /workspace folder inside the image
WORKDIR /workspace

# Put the packages in /opt/venv (not in a .venv folder in /workspace)
ENV UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv

# Copy only the files that list your packages
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock .python-version ./

# Install Python and the exact packages in uv.lock
# (--locked: stop if uv.lock doesn't match pyproject.toml)
RUN uv sync --locked
```

## renv (R)

```{.dockerfile filename="Dockerfile"}
# Adapted from docker-uv-renv by Daniel Chen (MIT License)
# https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv

# Start from Ubuntu Linux with R installed.
# Change 4.6.2 to the R version in your renv.lock.
FROM rocker/r-ver:4.6.2

# Install curl: renv downloads packages with it
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install --yes curl

# Work in the /workspace folder inside the image
WORKDIR /workspace

# Put the packages in /opt/renv/library (not in renv/library in /workspace)
RUN echo "RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY=/opt/renv/library" >> /usr/local/lib/R/etc/Renviron.site

# Copy only the files renv needs to install your packages
COPY DESCRIPTION renv.lock .Rprofile ./
COPY renv/activate.R renv/

# Install the exact packages in renv.lock
RUN Rscript -e "renv::restore()"
```
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Commands to test your image (step 4)

Open Docker Desktop first. From your repository folder, build the image and give it a name (`--tag`):

```bash
docker build --tag dsci522-test .
```

Then start a container, load your packages, and remove the container when it finishes (`--rm`).
Replace the package names with yours.
If nothing prints, it worked: an error means a package didn't install.

::: panel-tabset
## uv (Python)

```bash
docker run --rm dsci522-test uv run python -c "import cowsay, pyjokes"
```

## renv (R)

```bash
docker run --rm dsci522-test Rscript -e "library(cowsay); library(praise)"
```
:::

Changed your environment? Run `docker build` again: Docker rebuilds only the steps that changed.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The workflow file (step 5)

Change only the `IMAGE` line. The comments explain the rest.

```{.yaml filename=".github/workflows/publish-dockerhub.yml"}
# Builds the image from your Dockerfile and publishes it on Docker Hub.
# Save this file as .github/workflows/publish-dockerhub.yml

name: Publish image to Docker Hub

# When the workflow runs
on:
  # by hand: Actions tab > Publish image to Docker Hub > Run workflow
  workflow_dispatch:
  # on its own: when a push changes one of these files
  push:
    paths:
      - Dockerfile
      - uv.lock
      - renv.lock
      - .github/workflows/publish-dockerhub.yml

env:
  # CHANGE THIS LINE: your Docker Hub username / repository name, in lowercase
  IMAGE: your-docker-hub-username/dsci522-dockerfile-practice

jobs:
  publish:
    # a fresh Linux computer on GitHub (Intel/AMD)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # 1. Copy your repository onto that computer
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # 2. Log in to Docker Hub with your two repository secrets
      - name: Log in to Docker Hub
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}

      # 3. Build the image with two tags:
      #    latest, and sha- plus the first 7 characters of the commit ID
      - name: Build the image
        run: docker build --tag "$IMAGE:latest" --tag "$IMAGE:sha-${GITHUB_SHA::7}" .

      # 4. Upload both tags to Docker Hub
      - name: Push the image
        run: docker push --all-tags "$IMAGE"
```

Steps 3 and 4 are the same `docker build` and `docker push` you would type on your own computer:
GitHub just runs them for you, from the files in your repository.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Setting up Docker Hub and the GitHub secrets (step 5)

1.  Create a free [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/) account if you don't have one.
2.  Create a **public** Docker Hub repository named `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`.
3.  Create a Docker Hub [access token](https://docs.docker.com/security/access-tokens/) with Read & Write permissions.
    Copy it somewhere safe: you can only see it once.
4.  In your GitHub repository, add two
    [repository secrets](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets)
    (Settings \> Secrets and variables \> Actions \> New repository secret),
    with exactly these names, because the workflow looks for them:
    -   `DOCKER_USERNAME`: your Docker Hub username
    -   `DOCKER_PASSWORD`: the access token (**not** your Docker Hub password)
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Troubleshooting

-   **Git refuses to push the workflow file:** your personal access token needs the **workflow** scope.
    On GitHub, go to Settings \> Developer settings \> Personal access tokens, select your token, and tick **workflow**.
-   **The workflow didn't start:** it only starts on its own when a push changes the `Dockerfile`, a lock file or the workflow file.
    Run it by hand: **Actions** tab \> **Publish image to Docker Hub** \> **Run workflow**.
-   **The login step fails:** check the secret names, and that `DOCKER_PASSWORD` is an access token with Read & Write permissions.
-   **The push step fails with "denied" or "unauthorized":** the `IMAGE` line must start with your Docker Hub username, all in lowercase.
:::
